review_notes: I read the whole file, lines 1–93. It has two helper lemmas in `AnnCount2` and one main theorem, `solution`. None of them carries a `@[simp]` attribute, and the file declares no custom simp set. The only simp calls are local ones. Inside `sum_eq_zero_of_translate`, `simp` closes the goals `-g + (g + x) = x` and `g + (-g + x) = x`. In `solution`, `simp only [Set.mem_setOf_eq, Finset.coe_filter, memX]` and `memA` rewrite set-builder membership into filter membership. These are plain closing or normalizing uses. I saw no competing rules, no rewrite in an unsuitable direction, no unwanted expansion and no plausible loop. `sum_eq_card_of_forall_eq_one` is a one-off helper with a hypothesis `∀ x ∈ s, f x = 1`, so it would be a poor simp lemma. `sum_eq_zero_of_translate` has side conditions that simp could not discharge. Most of the file uses explicit `rw` chains and `exact_mod_cast`. Those are proof-style choices and not simp-interface defects. I did not search the dependencies for lemmas the file might duplicate. That question belongs to a different rubric, and I found no simp-specific issue that would need it.
